      {"@context":"http://schema.org","@graph":[{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-07-09T00:56:15.073Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_nau-mai-ng%C4%81-hua-o-tupu-%C4%81-nuku-o-tupu-%C4%81-rangi-activity-7480786865776832512-TSL9","text":"Nau mai ngā hua o Tupu-ā-nuku, o Tupu-ā-rangi, o Waitī, o Waitā.
I tīkina I te wao tapu nui a Tāne
Miromiro e Tāne 
Koakoa te tini a Tangaroa 
Nau mai Matariki heri kai 
Haramai te toki 
Haumi e hui e tāiki e!

There's no better way to celebrate Matariki, the Māori New Year, than with good kai, great company, and meaningful kōrero and that's exactly what our kaimahi in Tāmaki Makaurau did today.

Ahead of the long weekend, we joined our neighbours RNZ and Sunpix Ltd to share kai and learn more about the meaning of Matariki. It was a fitting reflection of this year's theme, 'Matariki herenga waka' which encourages us to come together, strengthen our connections, and celebrate the diverse communities that make up Aotearoa. 

Tomorrow morning, Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei will host the national Matariki Hautapu ceremony at Takaparawhau Bastion Point. With calm and clear weather on the way, the pre-dawn celebration will be a beautiful way to welcome the Māori New Year. You can watch the ceremony live on TVNZ 1 or TVNZ+.

Mānawatia a Matariki 🌟💫 ✨ ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_nau-mai-ng%C4%81-hua-o-tupu-%C4%81-nuku-o-tupu-%C4%81-rangi-activity-7480786865776832512-TSL9"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-07-06T21:46:40.980Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_meet-donald-allison-carnie-a-sports-producer-activity-7480014383633498112-fvco","text":"Meet Donald Allison-Carnie, a sports producer at TVNZ and an absolute legend🏏⚽
 
Working in sports at TVNZ is part of his DNA – his first job was right here working part-time during high school as a production assistant on Sunday Grandstand, where his father Murray Allison was a sports producer. He was also in charge of listening to local cricket updates and updating the scores to Richard Long for his sports news bulletins. Even his sister had a stint working at TVNZ!
 
Donald’s first full-time role at TVNZ started in 1988, where he was a television assistant. In 1989 he moved to be a tape operator, where he was responsible for getting programmes ready for transmission. He later moved into a sports specialist role, working on sports highlights and replays, live at events.

In 1993, the All Blacks took on the British Lions at Eden Park, and Donald was on replay duty. Frank Bunce scored a try, and in the excitement, Donald accidentally sent the replay into high speed, so the whole country watched Frank's try in double time! 10 years later, whilst in Invercargill for the National Bank Cup the match was repeated on TV and he got to watch Frank’s high speed try, once again! 
 
Currently, he's a sports producer, which requires a lot of planning ahead of events, working closely with sports rights holders, crew and making editorial decisions. During his time at TVNZ, he's worked on: 

🏆 6 Commonwealth Games 
🥇 5 Olympics 
🏅 7 Paralympics 
🏏 8 Black Clash events 

On why he loves working at TVNZ after 38 years, Donald said: "It's the people – we're all striving to do the best that we can and making each programme a great show for the viewer at home. It's also the sport – I'm very fortunate for a job that has involved travel, like working on the America's Cup in Valencia in 2007. Growing up, I saw my dad working here, so wanted to follow in his footsteps!"
 
Donald's 38 years shows what a career in sport at TVNZ can look like. If you have a love of sports and would love the opportunity to work with him (who wouldn't!), we're looking for our new GM of Sport, Events & Partnerships, as Melodie Robinson heads off to the big Apple. This win belongs to our incredible teams, our agency and commercial partners, and everyone who has backed us, challenged us and helped us keep pushing forward. We’re proud of what’s been achieved and even more excited about what’s ahead.
 
Congratulations to all the winners and finalists, and a huge thank you to the Commercial Communications Council, judges and sponsors for a fantastic Beacon Awards night. Alongside Minister Paul Goldsmith, Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, and kaimahi from both TVNZ and RNZ, we came together for a pōwhiri before catching up over kai.
 
While TVNZ and RNZ each have their own voice and identity, we are connected by a shared commitment to serving New Zealanders. Through the stories we tell, the voices we amplify and the communities we connect, that purpose is at the heart of what we do.
 
We’re excited to have the RNZ team here, and we hope they quickly feel right at home.

📸 Renata Blair - Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei 
📸 Bernadette Kelly - TVNZ Chief People & Corporate Officer","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_this-morning-we-marked-a-special-moment-at-activity-7476108936404869121-qPy7"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-06-23T03:21:30.145Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_last-week-tvnz-celebrated-samoan-language-activity-7475025213546610688-0DGC","text":"Last week, TVNZ celebrated Samoan Language Week in a very special way...

Introduced by our very own Barbara Dreaver, ONZM, the beautiful choral arrangement -performed in Samoan and Tongan - brought us together to celebrate the richness of our Pasifika community.

A huge fa’afetai lava to the talented performers from Auckland Girls’ Grammar School for sharing their voices, energy and culture with us. It was an uplifting and unforgettable way to finish the week. 👏 👏 👏 ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_last-week-tvnz-celebrated-samoan-language-activity-7475025213546610688-0DGC"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-06-18T00:12:31.508Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_the-all-whites-fifa-world-cup-2026-campaign-activity-7473165716528189440-PYIE","text":"The All Whites FIFA World Cup 2026™ campaign kicked off with record streaming on TVNZ+!

An epic performance from the team in their opening match saw TVNZ+ deliver its largest streaming day ever on 16 June, with almost 2.3 million streams on the platform across the 24-hour period.

The match, which resulted in a 2-2 draw against IR Iran, generated a massive 555,000 streams on TVNZ+. On TVNZ 1, 465,000 people watched the game, placing it in the top five highest-rated football matches on broadcast television since 2010.

Some of our TVNZ whānau watched the action unfold at Eden Park alongside our trade partners (and Plussie, of course!). Back at our Auckland headquarters, we got behind the team from our own makeshift football field.

The nail-biter match was a great reminder of the excitement the FIFA World Cup can bring, and the hard work happening behind the scenes to deliver the world’s largest sporting event to screens across Aotearoa.

Every All Whites match will be available free-to-air on TVNZ 1, and fans can watch the full tournament on TVNZ+ with an Event Pass.

Bring on Monday, when the All Whites take on Egypt in their second group stage match!","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_the-all-whites-fifa-world-cup-2026-campaign-activity-7473165716528189440-PYIE"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-06-11T00:58:24.745Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_were-proud-to-see-tvnz-hold-on-to-a-4th-activity-7470640549419483136-vyvr","text":"We’re proud to see TVNZ hold on to a 4th place position in the 2026 Kantar Corporate Reputation Index - a fantastic recognition of the mahi happening right across our business every day.

Congratulations to all the businesses recognised this year, especially the top three: Toyota New Zealand Limited, PAK'nSAVE and AA Insurance NZ. Thanks to Wright Communications (New Zealand) and Kantar for continuing to spotlight corporate reputation in Aotearoa. 📸 Our CEO Jodi O'Donnell picking up the award 👏 👏 👏   ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_were-proud-to-see-tvnz-hold-on-to-a-4th-activity-7470640549419483136-vyvr"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-06-10T04:59:10.649Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_at-tvnz-we-love-creating-space-for-budding-activity-7470338752037548032-e-Xj","text":"At TVNZ, we love creating space for budding journos to grow their skills and tell meaningful stories here in Aotearoa.

They did the hard mahi - pitching the story, securing interviews, capturing footage, writing the script, and editing the final piece.

It was the culmination of a huge amount of effort from the students, supported by lecturer Gregory Treadwell and guided by the experience of one of our fantastic journalists Laura Tupou.

A great example of what can happen when industry and education come together!","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_at-tvnz-we-love-creating-space-for-budding-activity-7470338752037548032-e-Xj"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TVNZ","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tvnz"},"datePublished":"2026-05-14T00:48:12.309Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tvnz_this-week-marked-the-launch-of-bnz-business-activity-7460491120431693825-GeTq","text":"This week marked the launch of BNZ Business Breakfast - our brand-new weekday business programme hosted by Mei Heron.

It’s been a big first week, with discussions ranging from the Singapore and New Zealand agreement on essential supplies, how AI search tools are using LinkedIn for business discoverability, to insights into the economic trends influencing Kiwi businesses right now. 

We’re incredibly proud to partner with Bank of New Zealand on this brand-new programme. BNZ Business Breakfast will continue to bring expert analysis and important conversations to audiences each morning, helping break down the news that matters most.  And thank you to Hearts & Science

Tomorrow morning, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/ngati-whatua-orakei-whai-maia-limited?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei</a> will host the national Matariki Hautapu ceremony at Takaparawhau Bastion Point. With calm and clear weather on the way, the pre-dawn celebration will be a beautiful way to welcome the Māori New Year. Mānawatia a Matariki 🌟💫 ✨ </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Meet Donald Allison-Carnie, a sports producer at TVNZ and an absolute legend🏏⚽
 
Working in sports at TVNZ is part of his DNA – his first job was right here working part-time during high school as a production assistant on Sunday Grandstand, where his father Murray Allison was a sports producer. He was also in charge of listening to local cricket updates and updating the scores to Richard Long for his sports news bulletins. Even his sister had a stint working at TVNZ!
 
Donald’s first full-time role at TVNZ started in 1988, where he was a television assistant. In 1989 he moved to be a tape operator, where he was responsible for getting programmes ready for transmission. He later moved into a sports specialist role, working on sports highlights and replays, live at events.

In 1993, the All Blacks took on the British Lions at Eden Park, and Donald was on replay duty. Frank Bunce scored a try, and in the excitement, Donald accidentally sent the replay into high speed, so the whole country watched Frank's try in double time! 10 years later, whilst in Invercargill for the National Bank Cup the match was repeated on TV and he got to watch Frank’s high speed try, once again! 
 
Currently, he's a sports producer, which requires a lot of planning ahead of events, working closely with sports rights holders, crew and making editorial decisions. During his time at TVNZ, he's worked on: 

🏆 6 Commonwealth Games 
🥇 5 Olympics 
🏅 7 Paralympics 
🏏 8 Black Clash events 

On why he loves working at TVNZ after 38 years, Donald said: "It's the people – we're all striving to do the best that we can and making each programme a great show for the viewer at home. It's also the sport – I'm very fortunate for a job that has involved travel, like working on the America's Cup in Valencia in 2007. Growing up, I saw my dad working here, so wanted to follow in his footsteps!"
 
Donald's 38 years shows what a career in sport at TVNZ can look like. If you have a love of sports and would love the opportunity to work with him (who wouldn't!), we're looking for our new GM of Sport, Events & Partnerships, as <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/melodierobinson?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Melodie Robinson</a> heads off to the big Apple.     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">The All Whites FIFA World Cup 2026™ campaign kicked off with record streaming on TVNZ+!

An epic performance from the team in their opening match saw TVNZ+ deliver its largest streaming day ever on 16 June, with almost 2.3 million streams on the platform across the 24-hour period.

The match, which resulted in a 2-2 draw against IR Iran, generated a massive 555,000 streams on TVNZ+. On TVNZ 1, 465,000 people watched the game, placing it in the top five highest-rated football matches on broadcast television since 2010.

Some of our TVNZ whānau watched the action unfold at Eden Park alongside our trade partners (and Plussie, of course!). Back at our Auckland headquarters, we got behind the team from our own makeshift football field.

The nail-biter match was a great reminder of the excitement the FIFA World Cup can bring, and the hard work happening behind the scenes to deliver the world’s largest sporting event to screens across Aotearoa.

Every All Whites match will be available free-to-air on TVNZ 1, and fans can watch the full tournament on TVNZ+ with an Event Pass.

Bring on Monday, when the All Whites take on Egypt in their second group stage match!</p>
